 Judgment

Plaintiff Nos.1 to 4 have preferred this appeal being aggrieved by the judgment and decree dated 19.04.2017 passed in O.S No.1454/2006 on the file of the learned IV Additional Senior Civil Judge,
Mysuru (hereinafter referred to as 'trial Court' for brevity), dismissing the suit of the plaintiffs for partition and separate possession of the suit schedule property with cost, which was confirmed in R.A.No.176/2017 on the file of the learned VII Additional District Judge, Mysuru (hereinafter referred to as 'First Appellate Court' for brevity) vide judgment dated 05.07.2018.
2. For the sake of convenience, parties are referred to as per their status and rank before the Trial Court.

3. Brief facts of the case are that, plaintiff Nos.1 to 4 have filed the suit O.S No.1454/2006 before the Trial Court against defendant Nos.1 to 4 seeking partition and separate possession of their 1/3 share in the schedule properties, to render account and for mesne profits.
Ten agricultural properties are described in the schedule appended to the plaint.
During the pendency of the suit, defendant Nos.5 to 17 were impleaded and suit schedule properties i.e., item Nos.11 to 15 were also included.
4. It is contended by the plaintiffs that plaintiff No.1 is the wife and plaintiff Nos.2 to 4 are the children of late Nanjundegowda @ Nanjundappa, who died in the year 1981.
Nanjundegowda is the son of late Puttegowda, who had three sons and one daughter.
Defendant No.1 is the first son of Puttegowda by name Channaankegowda.
Defendant No.1(a) is his wife and defendant No.1(b) and defendant Nos.5 and 6 are their children.
The third son of Puttegowda is late Muddegowda.
Defendant No.2 is his wife and defendant Nos.10, 12, 13 and 15 are their children.
Defendant No.17 is the daughter of late Puttegowda.

Defendant No.11 is the wife of defendant No.10 and Defendant No.14 is the wife of defendant No.13.
5.
It is stated that Puttegowda died several years ago, when his sons were still minors.
The joint family properties were being managed by Smt.Puttamma, the wife of late Puttegowda.

Therefore,
khata in respect of item Nos.1 to 3 were standing in the name of late Puttamma, who died on 22.06.1996.

Defendant No.17- Smt. Shivamma married long back and is residing separately for more Smt. Jayamma vs Smt. Nagarathnamma on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57203001/
5 than 15 years.
Item Nos.1 to 3 were yielding very good income and out of the income derived from the joint family properties, item Nos.4 to 7 were acquired in the names of members of the joint family.
Therefore, even item Nos.4 to 7 are the joint family properties.
6. It is further contended that defendant No.1 being the eldest member of the joint family was managing the affairs of the family and also the suit schedule properties.
The plaintiffs were kept in dark about the affairs of the joint family and also the income derived from the suit schedule properties.
Defendant No.1 in collusion with revenue official manipulated the entries in RTC and other revenue records pertaining to the suit schedule properties.
However, the plaintiffs are having 1/3 share over the suit schedule properties, they being the Class-I legal heirs of late Nanjundegowda.
7. It is contended that defendant No.1 was not rendering accounts, but usurping the entire income from the joint family properties.
Taking undue advantage of revenue documents standing in his name, item Nos. 4 to 9 of the suit schedule properties have been sold in favour of defendant Nos.3 and 4.
The said sale was not for family necessities.
Therefore, the said sale is not binding on the plaintiffs.

8. It is contended that after the death of Muddegowda, the plaintiffs demanded defendant No.1 to effect partition and allot their 1/4 share in the suit schedule properties by metes and bounds, but he started postponing partitioning the properties.
In the meantime, few items of the properties were notified for acquisition by Karnataka Industrial Area Development Board (hereinafter referred to as 'KIADB' for brevity).
Since the revenue documents were standing in the name of defendant No.1, he attempted to withdraw the compensation amount.
The plaintiffs contended that they are having 1/3 share over the compensation awarded for acquisition of the properties.
It is said that the cause of action for the suit arose on 16.11.2006 and prayed for partition and separate possession of plaintiffs 1/3 share, to render accounts along with mesne profits and costs.
9. Defendant No.1 appeared before the Trial Court and filed written statement denying the contentions taken by the plaintiffs.
It is contended that suit is bad for both mis-joinder and non-joinder of necessary parties.
The relationship between the parties are admitted, but the contention that plaintiff No.1 and defendant No.2 constitute Joint Hindu Family is denied.

It is contended that Nanjundegowda the husband of plaintiff No.1 and father of other plaintiffs got divided the family properties with defendant Nos.1 and 2 and was enjoying his share separately since long back.
It is admitted that late Puttegowda had three sons and a daughter as contended by the plaintiffs.
It is also admitted that after the death of Puttegowda, Smt.Puttamma was managing the affairs of the family.
The contention of the plaintiffs that khata in respect of item Nos.1 to 3 of the suit schedule properties were standing in the name of Late Puttamma, is denied.

It is contended that item Nos.1 and 2 of the suit schedule properties were the self-acquired properties of Puttamma and item No.3 was the ancestral property of the plaintiffs and defendant Nos.1 and 2.
It is stated that late Nanjundegowda, the father of Plaintiff Nos.2 to 4 during his life time, took his share in item No.10 and other properties and started living separately.
Two RCC houses were also fallen to his share.
The house situated at Yelwala is let-out by the plaintiffs and they are getting the income.
The properties that were allotted to the share of Nanjundegowda was more valuable than the other properties.
Those properties were deliberately not included in the suit schedule.

Therefore, it is contended that the properties held by the family was already partitioned and the plaintiffs are not having any right, title and interest over the suit schedule properties.
10. Defendant No.1 contended that since from the date of division, the brothers started residing separately and were enjoying their respective shares.
It is admitted that item Nos.4 to 8 of the suit schedule properties were sold in favour of defendant No.3.
Item No.8 of the suit schedule property is the self acquired property of defendant No.1 and no one else had any right over the same.
11. It is contended that Survey Nos.169/1, 169/2, 169/3, 170/3, 120/1, and 110 have been acquired by KIADB and prior to the acquisition, the said properties were sold.
Defendant No.3 was in possession of the said property being the purchaser.
Muddegowda, the husband of defendant No.2 also sold some of the properties in favour of defendant No.4 during his life time.
Therefore, the Court fee paid by the plaintiffs is not proper and plaintiffs are not entitled for any share over the suit schedule property.
Accordingly, he prays for dismissal of the suit.

12. Defendant No.1 filed the additional written statement contending that item No.11 of the suit schedule property had fallen to the share of Muddegowda, the husband of defendant No.2 and he sold it in favour of one Munigowda.
The said Munigowda in turn sold the property in favour of one Madhusudan during 1990.
Thus, the said Madusudan is in possession and enjoyment of item No.11 of the suit schedule property.
Similarly, it is contended that item No.12 of the suit schedule property is included in item No.6 and the said property was already sold to one Manjunatha by the defendant.
Therefore, the said Manjunatha is in possession of the property.
13. Defendant No.2 filed the written statement denying the contentions taken by the plaintiffs.
It is admitted that the parties are Hindus and plaintiffs and defendants constitute Hindu Joint Family.
The relationship between the parties are admitted.
It is contended that the plaintiffs have intentionally suppressed the true and correct facts to make wrongful gain.
It is stated that during the life time of Puttamma, the joint family properties were partitioned between her sons.
The said Puttamma had purchased item Nos.1 and 2 and the revenue records were standing in her name.
Puttamma effected partition of the properties between her sons Muddegowda and defendant No.1.
Husband of plaintiff No.1 was given properties situated at Hunsur i.e., the wet land which was more fertile, along with the house situated at Yelwala and also cash.
This partition was effected about 25 years ago and the plaintiffs are well aware of these facts.
Since there was already a partition of the family properties, the plaintiffs are not having any shares over the suit schedule property.
Accordingly, he prays for dismissal of the suit.
14. Defendant No.4 filed written statement denying the contentions taken by the plaintiffs.
It is contended that defendant No.4 is not having any interest in any of the suit schedule property, except item No.9.
The said property was originally belonging to Smt. H.S.Jayashree who acquired it from Muddegowda under a sale deed.
Said Smt.H.S.Jayashree sold the property in favour of one E.Ningamma for valuable consideration during 1995, who is none other than the mother of defendant No.4.
Thus, Ningamma become the absolute owner in possession of the property.

She executed a registered gift deed in favour of defendant No.4 on 23.01.2002 and since then defendant Smt. Jayamma vs Smt. Nagarathnamma on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57203001/

The plaintiffs are not in joint possession of item No.9 and therefore, the Court fee paid is not sufficient.

Hence, defendant No.4 prays for dismissal of suit in respect of item No.9.
15.
Defendant Nos.5 and 6 have filed their written statement admitting their relationship with defendant No.1.
However, contended that the suit of the plaintiffs is not maintainable for non-joinder of necessary parties.

It is also contended that the plaintiffs are not included the properties that were allotted to the share of Nanjundegowda i.e., wet land bearing Survey No.147/2A situated at Uddur Nala, Hunsur measuring 2.20 acres which was purchased by Puttamma in the name of Nanjundegowda and plaintiff No.1, and Survey No.190/40B situated at Dodda Hunsur village measuring 2.00 acres, RCC roofed house bearing property No.834 situated at Hunsur town measuring 80/45 feet , 2 floored RCC building bearing No.73/2 with vacant site situated at Yelwala village and the revenue house within Mysuru city in addition to plaint schedule item No.10.
Item No.10 alone was valuing 4 or 5 times more than the total value of the properties allotted to the share of Muddegowda and defendant No.1.
The RCC building was also more valuable.
16. It is contended that item Nos.1 and 2 of the plaint schedule properties were already sold by defendant No.2 and her children.
Similarly, item Nos.4 and 5 were also sold in favour of one Nagendra in the year 2005.

Defendant Nos.5 and 6 have sold 17 guntas and 18 guntas respectively,
from out of item Nos.6 and 7 in favour of the said Nagendra.

Item No.8 was also sold by defendant No.1 in favour of Nagendra during 1994-95.
17.

It is further contended that the legal representatives of late Muddegowda i.e., defendant No.2 and her children sold 5.25 acres of land in item No.1 of the plaint schedule and 1.30 acres in Survey No.107, which is not included in the plaint schedule in the year 1991 in the favour of defendant Nos.3 and 4 and in favour of Ginigowda, Vishakanta and Madhusudan respectively.
Defendant No.2 and her children have also sold portion of the properties in item Nos.1 and 2 in favour of M/s. Sky Top builders and sold item No.11 in the year 2000 in favour of one Nagaraju.

18. It is contended that plaint schedule item Nos.12 to 15 are the self acquired properties of defendant Nos.5 and 6 as they purchased the said items in the year 1993-94 and already sold the same after getting it converted in favour of one Hussain Ali Qureshi.
From out of their earnings they acquired item Nos. 11, 13 and 14 and the plaintiffs are not having any right over the same.

19. It is contended that none of the properties are available for partition and the plaintiffs having any share whatsoever the plaintiffs have not sought for declaration in respect of various alienations made long back and the suit is not properly valued.
The suit is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties.
Their similar prayer in O.S No.557/2010 was already rejected.
It is also contended that suit is barred by limitation.
Hence, they pray for dismissal of the suit.
20. Defendant No.7 filed written statement denying the contentions of the plaintiffs.

It is contended that he purchased Survey No.98/01 measuring 3.09 acres and Sy.No.115 measuring 2.26 acres of Karakanahalli village from defendant No.9 as GPA holder of defendant Nos.2, 10 to 15 under the registered sale deed executed during May 2010.

It is also contended that after purchase of the property, defendant No.7 converted the land for non- agricultural purpose and they formed the layout after obtaining the sanctioned plan from MUDA by investing huge amount.
Therefore, he prays for dismissal of the suit.
21. Defendant No.17 filed written statement admitting the contentions taken by the plaintiffs and stated that she has no objection to decree the suit in respect of the suit schedule properties.

23. Plaintiff No.3 examined himself as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to 60 in support of his contention.
The defendants got examined DWs.1 to 7 and got marked Exs.D.1 to 69 in support of their contention.

The Trial Court after taking into consideration all these materials on record, answered issue Nos.1, 4, 5 , 6 and additional issue No.3 in the affirmative and issue Nos.2 , 3 , 7, 8, and additional issue Nos. 1 and 2 in the negative, in the result dismissed the suit of the plaintiffs with cost.
24.
Being aggrieved by the same, the plaintiff Nos.1 to 4 have preferred R.A No.176/2017.

The First Appellate Court on re-appreciation of the materials on record,
dismissed the appeal confirming the impugned judgment and decree passed by the trial Court.
Being aggrieved by the same, the plaintiffs have preferred this appeal.
25. Learned counsel for the appellants contended that the relationship between the parties is categorically admitted by the defendants.
The defendants have taken a defence that there was an earlier partition in the family as per Ex.D14.
Ex.D.14 is an unregistered document which cannot be relied on.
It is only Puttamma, the grandmother of plaintiff Nos.2 to 4 had signed the document.
Nanjundegowda, the father of plaintiff Nos.2 to 4 is not a party to the said document.
Puttamma was not a coparcener to enter into partition or to effect partition in respect of the family properties.
26. Learned counsel further submitted that item Nos.1 to 7 are the family properties acquired by defendants from out of the joint family nuclues.
The defendants were not having any absolute right, title or interest to alienate the said properties.
The transferees have not acquired any title on these items, as neither the father of plaintiff Nos.2 to 4 nor the plaintiffs have joined in execution of such sale deeds.

When the schedule properties were originally belonging to Puttegowda, who is the propositors and the relationship between the parties is admitted, the Trial Court and the First Appellate Court committed an error in dismissing the suit.
The contention taken by the defendants that the father of plaintiff Nos.2 to 4 were allotted different properties are not proved.
There is no reference to Ex.D.14 in any of the sale deeds.
Therefore, it is clear that Ex.D.14 is a sham document, which was never acted upon.
In the absence of Ex.D.14, the defendants were not having any right, title or interest to execute the sale deed in respect of any of the items of the properties.
The plaintiffs being the wife and children of late Nanjundegowda are entitled for 1/3rd share in the schedule properties.
The sale deeds executed behind the back of the plaintiffs will not take away their right over the properties.
Therefore, learned counsel prays for allowing the appeal by setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the First Appellate Court, in the interest of justice.

28. In view of the contentions taken by the appellants, the following substantial question of law was formulated vide order dated 21.12.2020:
"Whether the Courts below have committed an error in dismissing the suit relying on the unregistered Palu-Parikath signed only by the wife of the kartha of Hindu Undivided family and without considering the evidence placed on record?"
29.
Perused the materials including the Trial Court Records in light of the submissions made by the learned counsel for the appellants.

30. It is the specific contention of the plaintiffs that Nanjundegowda, the husband of plaintiff No.1 and father of other plaintiffs was the son of the propositor late Puttegowda and his wife Puttamma.
Nanjundegowda had two brothers i.e., Channaankegowda- defendant No.1 and Muddegowda - husband of defendant No.2 and one sister by name Shivamma- defendant No.17.
The relationship between the parties is not in dispute.
The contesting defendants even though filed written statements separately, their common defence is that there was an earlier partition in the family as evidenced by Ex.D.14 dated 10.05.1983.
This document is described as Memorandum of partition or Panchayat Palu- Parikath.
The recitals in the document also disclose there was a Panchayat held in the presence of panchayatdars and the properties were divided amongst the children of Puttegowda and Puttamma.
Schedule II referred to in Ex.D.14 describes the properties that were allotted to the share of Nanjundegowda and Jayamma i.e., plaintiff No.1 and her husband.
The defendants have stated in the written statement that Nanjundegowda after taking the properties mentioned in Ex.D.14, separated himself with his family and was residing at Hunsur.
It is also their contention that the defendants have taken their respective shares and acquired some of the items of the properties and sold some of the items in favour of third parties.
31. Plaintiff No.3 is examined as PW.3 on behalf of all the plaintiffs and got marked several documents.

From the evidence of this witness, it is clear that Nanjundegowda was residing separately and had never claimed any share in the properties that were being enjoyed by his brothers Channaankegowda and Muddegowda.

The witness also admits that the properties that are referred to in schedule-B to Ex.D.14 were in fact enjoyed by Nanjundegowda, but he contends that those were the properties acquired by Nanjundegowda by different means.
However, the plaintiffs have not produced any document to substantiate the contention that those documents were acquired by Nanjundegowda in any other manner other than under Ex.D.14.

When it is the specific contention of the plaintiffs that Ex.D.14 was not the document evidencing the partition between the brothers, there is no explanation as to how the properties that were in possession of Nanjundegowda could find a place in Ex.D.14.
PW.1 categorically admits during cross examination that a house property was given to their family and half portion in the RCC building was given in favour of Muddegowda.
It is a matter of record that Muddegowda and his wife and children sold that portion of the property that was allotted to his share under the partition.

Smt. Jayamma vs Smt. Nagarathnamma on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57203001/
11 32.
Ex .D.14 is signed by Smt. Puttamma, the mother of Nanjundegowda.
Her left thumb impression mark is found on the document.
The plaintiffs have disputed this LTM of Puttamma.
However, it is contended that Puttamma was not the coparcener and she had no authority to effect partition.

But,
the fact remains that Puttamma being the eldest member of the family and moreover being the mother of Nanjundegowda, Channaankegowda and Muddegowda convened Panchayat and effected partition.
The partition was effected in the presence of panchayatdars, who have signed Ex.D.14.
Simply because, Ex.D.14 is an unregistered document and signed only by Puttamma, it will not make this document inadmissible.

This document was relied on by the defendants to prove their contention that there was already a partition, whereunder, Nanjundegowda through whom the plaintiffs are claiming title had acquired share over some of the properties.

The admissions on the part of PW.1 substantiate the contention of the defendants and also proves effecting of partition as evidenced in Ex.D.14.
33.
It is pertinent to note that Ex.D.14 is dated 10.05.1983.
The plaintiffs have filed the suit during 2006.
It is stated that Nanjundegowda died in the year 1981.
The recitals in Ex.D.14 disclose that Nanjundegowda had died prior to Ex.D.14 and it was plaintiff No.1, who represented her children during Panchayat.

If at all there was no partition as evidenced by Ex.D.14, there was absolutely no reason as to why the plaintiffs have not claimed their share over the family properties from 1981,
when Nanjundegowda died till 2006.
34. PW.1 pleads his ignorance about the sale or purchase of various properties by his uncle Channaankegowda or Muddegowda or their family members.
This also probabalises that the defence taken by the defendants about severance of status between the family members.
The oral and documentary evidence placed disclose that after the death of Puttegowda, for sometime the family was united and Puttamma was managing the affairs.
In the meantime, Nanjundegowda separated with his family and was doing business.
He died in the year 1981 and immediately thereafter, during 1983 a Panchayat was convened and the family properties were divided amongst the sharers by Puttamma.

Even though the right of Smt.Puttamma to effect partition amongst her sons, is being questioned at this length of time, it is also interesting to note that the documents produced before the Court including Ex.P.48 disclose that it was Smt.Puttamma, who acquired item Nos.1 and 2 of the schedule properties and the same was never disputed by any of the parties,
including the plaintiffs.
35. The documents produced before the Court disclose that many of the items of the property were sold and third party interest has been created.
Item Nos.4 to 8 were sold in favour of defendant No.3 and subsequently same was acquired by KIADB.
Defendant No.4 sold some of the properties.
There are several purchasers under different sale deeds some of whom are arrayed as defendants.
It is pertinent to note that defendant No.2 sold item Nos.1 and 2 of the schedule properties in favour of defendant No.7.
Challenging the sale the suit O.S.No.557/2010 was filed against defendant No.7.
Admittedly, the said suit came to be dismissed.
36. It is also pertinent to note that none of the sale transactions were challenged by the plaintiffs.
No declaration is sought in respect of the registered sale deeds that were entered into between Channaankegowda, Muddegowda or their family members.

In this regard, I may refer to the Smt. Jayamma vs Smt. Nagarathnamma on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57203001/
12 decision of the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in Sri U. Vijaya Kumar and Another vs. Smt.Malini V.Rao1, wherein, it is held that when the plaintiffs seek to establish their title and finds themselves threatened by a transaction between some parties, their remedy is to get a declaration that the said decree or deed or transaction is invalid so far as they are concerned.

entities.text: Sri U. Vijaya Kumar and Another vs. Smt.Malini V.Rao1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, if the plaintiffs are a party to the decree, deed or transaction, they have to get it cancelled by seeking necessary relief under law.

37. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Suhrid Singh alias Sardool Singh v. Randhir Singh and Others2,
while discussing about the court fee that is to be paid in a suit for declaratory relief with consequential relief for annulment of a deed, discussed at length about the relief that is to be claimed by the executant to the document vis-a-vis non-executant.

entities.text: Suhrid Singh alias Sardool Singh v. Randhir Singh and Others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
ILR 2016 KAR 2670 (2010) 12 SCC 112 The Hon'ble Apex Court in Para-7 of the judgment held as under:
"7. Where the executant of a deed wants it to be annulled, he has to seek cancellation of the deed.
But if a non-executant seeks annulment of a deed, he has to seek a declaration that the deed is invalid, or non-est, or illegal or that it is not binding on him.
The difference between a prayer for cancellation and declaration in regard to a deed of transfer/conveyance, can be brought out by the following illustration relating to A and B, two brothers.
A executes a sale deed in favour of C.
Subsequently A wants to avoid the sale.
A has to sue for cancellation of the deed.

On the other hand, if B,
who is not the executant of the deed, wants to avoid it, he has to sue for a declaration that the deed executed by A is invalid/void and non-est/illegal and he is not bound by it.
In essence both may be suing to have the deed set aside or declared as non- binding.
But the form is different and court fee is also different.
38. Defendant No.17 is admittedly the daughter of late Puttegowda and Puttamma.
She had filed her written statement admitting the claim of plaintiffs and seeking her share in the schedule properties.
She was impleaded as defendant No.17 by the plaintiffs during pendency of the suit and at that time she was said to be aged 65 years.
Admittedly, she never claimed any right over the property.

There are sufficient materials to show that there was a partition in the family and on the basis of such partition several registered documents were came to be executed at an undisputed point of time and thereby creating third party interest.
The documents that are placed before the Court disclose that many of the schedule properties have lost their identity.
Ex.D.69 produced by defendant No.7 discloses that the property that was purchased by him was converted into non-agricultural land and residential layout is formed.
Similarly defendant Nos.5 and 6 have purchased few items of the property during 1993-94 and got converted the land and sold it in favour of others.
In view of all these facts and circumstances, the claim of the plaintiffs or defendant No.17 cannot be entertained.
39. The discussions held above disclose that the plaintiffs have failed to prove their contention regarding schedule properties.
The Trial Court and the First Appellate Court have considered the oral and documentary evidence led by the parties in detail and have arrived at a right conclusion.
I do not find any reason to form a different opinion to disturb the concurrent findings of the fact.
The substantial question of law formulated is answered against the appellants and in favour of the respondents.

ORDER (i) The appeal is dismissed with costs.
